claim: G31 P7 R1: Miter can construct and natively assess a complete, source-bound, human-reviewable but inactive Mattermost live-grant proposal that surfaces every C-098 permission and lifecycle boundary, retains actual identities privately, and cannot become live while its independent live-effect approval remains unresolved.
non_claims: No Mattermost network request, WebSocket, post/content read, message effect, live-effect approval, VoiceRNA execution, adapter activation/promotion, live canary, restart/panic proof, production readiness, model call, or G31 closure.
rationale: C-098 requires explicit human approval only after purpose, scope, permissions, persistence, ongoing access, reversibility and test evidence are surfaced. P5 and P6 establish exact identities and principal-selection authority but do not supply message authority. A versioned v3 representation must separate those facts before Berton can meaningfully approve, narrow or reject the live experiment.
reading: Retain both controls and the full G29-G31 lineage. Reread C-004-C-008/C-020-C-024/C-050-C-055/C-060-C-066/C-090-C-104; S-103/S-401-S-405/S-501-S-504/S-603/S-605/S-607/S-804/S-901-S-905/S-1004-S-1005/S-1101-S-1105/S-1201-S-1203; ACCEPTANCE G31; POC_SPEC 16-17; D-024-D-026/D-033-D-037; W-120-W-127; the exact P3 candidate, P4 transport closure, P5 identity closure, and P6 principal closure. Honor the user's standing instruction that no message be sent yet.
representation: Introduce `live-grant-v3` with distinct principal-selection-authority and live-effect-approval fields. Construct a private mode-0600 grant containing exact IDs and a public redacted proposal containing only hashes and opaque private references. Required fields include candidate/transport versions; purpose; server/team/allowlisted and denied-control scopes; authorized inbound principal; bot; Keychain capability; event/content exposure; outbound effect class and exact target; fixed canary text and bounded sequence; memory scope; VoiceRNA certificate route; reconciliation limits; cursor/effect journals; activation-relative expiry; no ongoing access beyond the experiment; panic; rollback; revocation; source evidence; principal authority; and unresolved live approval.
consumer: PeTTa/MeTTa owns grant construction meaning, completeness and held standing. A Prolog membrane may only materialize exact private references, hash/read back files and enforce restrictive storage; it cannot approve or activate. JavaScript freezes inputs, verifies private/public separation and exercises positive, severed, neutral and restored grant forms; it cannot contact Mattermost or grant reach.
falsifiers: Any required permission or lifecycle field is absent; v2 conflation of human identity and live-effect approval remains; actual IDs, username or credential enter Git; the inactive grant authorizes a network call; post-content exposure is hidden; denied-channel observation can enter cognition; memory scope is unspecified; VoiceRNA can be bypassed; expiry/ongoing access/panic/rollback/revocation is vague; a severed source or field passes; an unexecuted native expression passes; or any network, post, message, model, promotion or activation occurs.
scope_review: Add only the v3 inactive-grant ontology, private materialization mechanics, public review proposal, native causal trials, evidence, closure and next separately frozen plan. No Mattermost/Keychain call, message/content, candidate/transport edit, model, Docker mutation, promotion, activation, push or control change.
rollback: Delete the ignored P7 grant proposal and remove P7 ontology/probe/evidence additions. P5 identities, P6 principal binding, Keychain, Mattermost state, candidate and transport remain unchanged; no live effect exists.
